column2: An ordinary English noun for an underlying layer and a synthetic dependency/provider name, not a selected upstream implementation: SPEC.md describes an assumed research base; ROADMAP.md names base CI and a dependency-base fixture; crates/ravel-host-api/src/services.rs and crates/ravel-save/src/lib.rs use a generic base dependency in tests.

An ordinary English preposition describing filesystem containment: crates/ravel-package/src/integrity.rs documents verifying a source file's digest beneath the package root. This does not identify the selected upstream mod or its dimension.

The deliberately invalid mixed-case string exampleMod in crates/ravel-core/src/identity.rs tests that ModId rejects uppercase M at index 7. It is a synthetic identity-validation example, not a public upstream mod identity or implementation.

The ordinary crop action and a source-module name in docs/handoff/lane-registry-report.md's model/harvest maintenance note. The note describes replacing Ravel counterpart code's numeric sentinel with Option; it does not name or claim the selected upstream mod.

The ordinary programming adjective for multiple methods or constructors sharing a name: crates/ravel-minecraft-generate/src/stub_render.rs and stubs.rs describe constructor disambiguation and mapping/stub tests. These references concern JVM signatures, not the selected upstream mod.

The ordinary plural noun for process output: evidence/m3/linux-process-matrix.json describes sanitized stdout/log streams whose raw captures were deleted. This frozen evidence is about output redaction, not the selected upstream mod or its world-generation behaviour.
